title: AI Monk Avatars: A Field Guide to the Creators, Formats, and Money Paths
description: A cited starter directory of five AI monk avatar profiles, their creative formats and visible product paths, with evidence labels and unresolved questions.
markdown:
# AI Monk Avatars: A Field Guide to the Creators, Formats, and Money Paths

A monk in a short video can look like one simple idea. Public evidence shows several different operations: a disclosed AI character connected to a paid program, a monk-like health avatar linked to a guide, and accounts whose AI status or operator is not yet established. Treating all of them as one “AI monk business” hides the questions that matter: who made the persona, what viewers see, which product is offered, and whether any sales figure is actually verified.

This guide starts with five sourced records. It is a first edition of the Anicca AI Monk Avatars directory, not a census of every account. The accompanying [open JSON dataset](/data/ai-monk-avatar-database-2026.json) keeps the evidence strength and unknowns beside each profile.

## What counts as an AI monk avatar?

For this project, an AI monk avatar is a synthetic or AI-labelled monk-like persona used in social video. A robe, a temple background, or an older face alone does not establish AI generation. We separate three evidence labels:

- **Confirmed:** a creator/platform disclosure or credible reporting identifies the persona as AI-generated.
- **Reported:** a credible investigation classifies the account as AI-generated, but another source disputes or leaves the provenance uncertain.
- **Unverified:** the evidence is a screenshot or visual impression that has not been independently confirmed.

A living Buddhist teacher using a 2-D avatar belongs in a separate category. So does an animated parable whose description does not establish AI. These exclusions prevent us from inflating the size of the AI monk field.

## Timeline: the origin is not known

The Yang Mun YouTube screenshot supplied for this research shows a channel join date of 4 November 2025. YT-DLP also found Yang Mun Shorts uploaded later that month. Those dates tell us the channel and sampled clips existed; they do not prove when the character was conceived or who published the first AI monk video.

By 10 July 2026, Maldita.es had reported on 16 AI-generated Facebook and Instagram profiles, including Shaolin-style personas Leo Chen and SifuChen California. On 27 July it published a separate study of 250 AI-generated health profiles in seven languages. The study put 82 profiles into a broad “ancestral wisdom” category, which includes non-monks as well as monk-like characters. Neither article gives the account-launch dates needed to award a “first” title.

The careful history is therefore a sequence of documented snapshots, not a winner claim. We know Yang Mun became a high-profile case. We do not yet know which account originated the AI monk format.

## Five records in the starter directory

### Yang Mun — confirmed synthetic persona

HeyGen’s customer story and Columbia News Service identify Yang Mun as an AI character created by Shalev Hani. The Instagram profile is yangmunus and the YouTube channel is Yangmunv2. A profile study reports multiple TikTok accounts, but does not publish exact handles; the dataset leaves TikTok unresolved.

The official store lists a $49.99 30-Day Healing Journey and a $59.99 collection with three eBooks. Those are visible offers, not paid-order data. Columbia reports Hani’s statement of more than $300,000 in revenue since launch and a $325,000 acquisition offer. Virtual Humans reports a separate claim of more than $300,000 in profit within 90 days. The periods and accounting terms differ; neither report supplies an audited statement.

### Ming San — reported AI provenance; sources conflict

Maldita includes mingsanhealing in its AI-generated health-profile investigation. Its July 20–21 snapshot reported about 1.2 million followers and described a monk-like wellness persona. The supplied Instagram screenshot shows about 1.37 million followers and a beetroot product link. AvatarFactory’s own profile says it could not establish whether Ming San is AI. We label the provenance “reported” and preserve the conflicting sources.

The link is evidence of a visible product route. It does not establish an affiliate commission, a sale, or profit.

### SifuChen California — reported AI avatar with a guide path

Maldita’s July 2026 report describes SifuChen California as an AI-generated Shaolin-style character and notes a €16.45 guide promoted through a profile highlight. The report does not provide a verified live handle, order count, or earnings. The database keeps the archived profile link and leaves current account metrics blank.

### Leo Chen — reported AI indicators; identity unresolved

Maldita reports visual inconsistencies in a video attributed to Leo Chen and describes a comment-to-message path for a Chinese healing book or PDF. The article does not establish a verified handle or creator identity. Its 2.2 million view figure is attached to the reported video, not to verified sales.

### Yan Chen / monjechen — screenshot-only lead

A supplied Instagram screenshot shows the profile name “Yan Chen | Sabiduría sanadora,” an “AI-generated profile” label, about 1.34 million followers, and 584 posts. It also shows an external product URL, but the URL is cropped. Our public crawler could not independently read the full profile. This entry remains unverified until the label, full offer destination, and account identity are checked again.

## Two Yang Mun videos show distinct script structures

We used YT-DLP to enumerate 143 items in Yang Mun’s Shorts view and temporarily downloaded two public Shorts for local caption and frame analysis. The source videos are not hosted in this repository; the dataset stores public links and structural summaries.

[youtube-short:Er2Ig4GM7z0|Words of Motivation from Yang Mun]

The 65-second “Words of Motivation” clip is one uninterrupted, centered shot in a temple-like setting. Its script moves from future reassurance, through familiar hopes for work and relationships, to a small repeatable morning-and-night practice. The frame, robe, book, candles, voice, and pacing stay consistent. The video does not make a paid-product pitch.

A second, 78-second [Short](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Qdv6S7HonSM) begins with waking in the night and turns toward a traditional-medicine explanation. That video makes an unverified health claim. It is useful to study as a moderation and trust risk, not as a medical script to reproduce. A separate YouTube Short with a water-related title displayed roughly 12 million views in metadata; we did not download or fact-check it.

Across the other documented profiles, Maldita describes additional routes: an eBook requested through a comment keyword, a guide linked from a story highlight, and external wellness products. These are not all the same funnel.

## The recurring creative grammar

The sampled clips and reports point to several repeatable mechanics:

1. **A fast authority cue:** a monk-like appearance, temple setting, calm voice, or direct eye contact identifies the character before the viewer reads the caption.
2. **A familiar concern:** the opening refers to worry, sleep, health, loneliness, or a decision people already have in mind.
3. **One point per clip:** the video presents a single reflection, story, or explanation instead of a multi-topic lecture.
4. **A calm resolution:** it closes with a reframe, a small practice, or a simple next step.
5. **A separate conversion step:** a link in the bio, story highlight, comment response, or store page carries the offer.

The patterns are structural observations. The exact script, voice, face, robe, temple set, music, and line delivery belong to each creator. Anicca’s work uses original writing, an authorized fictional presenter, and claims grounded in our own materials.

## How the money paths differ

The starter records show at least four visible business routes:

- Yang Mun combines short-form videos with a paid 30-day program and an eBook bundle.
- SifuChen California promotes a paid digital guide, according to Maldita.
- Leo Chen is reported to offer a book or PDF after a comment prompt.
- Ming San’s supplied profile screenshot shows an external wellness-product link; sales and commission are unknown.

Maldita found visible product URLs on 224 of the 250 AI health profiles it studied. That is a count for its broad health-profile sample, not for AI monk avatars alone. A profile link proves that an offer is visible; only provider orders and settlement data prove a sale and its net contribution.

A separate GrowwStacks marketing article proposes an automation chain: select a topic in Airtable, draft with an LLM, generate an avatar video in HeyGen, add captions, schedule social posts, and log the result. HeyGen’s customer story separately reports Hani’s production-time and posting-frequency claims. Neither source confirms that GrowwStacks’ workflow is Yang Mun’s actual stack or independently verifies its cost estimates.

## Build a directory that can be corrected

The Anicca dataset stores public profile URLs, source records, evidence labels, visible offer types, dated audience snapshots, video links, and unresolved fields. It deliberately leaves missing TikTok handles and unverified profile owners blank. The next research pass can add records when it finds a public profile, an AI-provenance source, and a dated creative sample.

The project’s current evidence does not establish a complete account count, a first creator, revenue ranking, or net profit. The index is open so other researchers can add stronger primary sources and correct outdated snapshots. Start with the [downloadable JSON dataset](/data/ai-monk-avatar-database-2026.json), the [Yang Mun case study](https://aniccaai.com/blog/ebook-publishing-yang-mun-video-to-product), and the [AI Monk Avatars category hub](https://aniccaai.com/blog/c/ai-monk-avatars). Read the [Japanese field guide](https://aniccaai.com/blog/ai-monk-avatar-field-guide-ja-2026) and the bilingual [book outline in English](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca-products/blob/main/docs/books/the-monk-in-your-feed-outline-en.md) and [Japanese](https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca-products/blob/main/docs/books/the-monk-in-your-feed-outline-ja.md) too.

This work also feeds the bilingual book proposal, *The Monk in Your Feed*. The book follows the same evidence standard: cite the creator, separate the audience metric from the business result, and make the ethics visible.
